```{python}
# octavo:example start — fake data. Replace with code that reads yours, then delete
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
rng = np.random.default_rng(20260101)
d = pd.DataFrame({"x": rng.normal(12, 3, 1523), "y": rng.normal(50, 10, 1523)})
d["y"] = d["y"] + 0.34 * d["x"]
# octavo:example end

ov_value("n_obs", len(d), note="observations used in the analysis")
```

## Estimation

```{python}
#| label: model
# Coefficient, standard error, p-value. For real work use statsmodels or similar
# (add it to requirements.txt)
import math
x, y = d["x"].to_numpy(), d["y"].to_numpy()
b = np.cov(x, y, ddof=1)[0, 1] / x.var(ddof=1)
resid = y - (y.mean() + b * (x - x.mean()))
se = math.sqrt(resid.var(ddof=2) / ((x - x.mean()) ** 2).sum())
p = math.erfc(abs(b / se) / math.sqrt(2))       # a large sample, so the normal approximation

ov_value("coef_x", b)
ov_value("se_x", se)
ov_value("p_x", ov_pval(p))
```

Write `{{n_obs}}` `{{coef_x}}` `{{p_x}}` in the manuscript and these values go in.

## Figure

```{python}
#| label: fig-trend
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
ax.scatter(d["x"], d["y"], s=8, color=ov_tint(ov_palette(["blue"])[0], 0.4))
xs = np.array([x.min(), x.max()])
ax.plot(xs, y.mean() + b * (xs - x.mean()), color="black", linewidth=2)
ax.set_xlabel("x"); ax.set_ylabel("y")
fig.tight_layout()
ov_figure(fig, "trend")      # assets/figures/trend.pdf and .png
```

In the manuscript, write `![Trend](../../assets/figures/trend.png){#fig-trend}` and
refer to it as `@fig-trend` (it is numbered when typeset: Figure 2.1).

## Table

```{python}
#| label: tbl-summary
tab = pd.DataFrame({
    "Variable": ["x", "y"],
    "Mean": [x.mean(), y.mean()],
    "SD": [x.std(ddof=1), y.std(ddof=1)],
})
ov_table(tab, "summary", notes=f"Note: N = {len(d):,}.")
```

This writes the table's contents (assets/tables/summary.typ / .tex / .md). In the
manuscript, the one line `: Descriptive statistics {#tbl-summary}` puts it
there with its caption, and `@tbl-summary` refers to it.
